title: Hungarian B1
description: Dual-track B1: a Core grammar-and-topics track, plus a Citizenship track covering the Hungarian history, constitution, symbols and civic knowledge tested in the honosítási vizsga (simplified-naturalization citizenship interview). Same shape as the Spanish course's Core/LatAm-history split — see ROADMAP.md's 'Hungarian: introduce Hungarian cultural material at B1-B2 (for the citizenship exam)' note.
notes: Each unit gets 5 regular lessons (as listed) plus 1 consolidation lesson, matching the A1/A2 pattern.

Content pipeline: Core units should use numeric filenames (b1-core-01-01 style, or whatever numbering convention lessons.js's HU path expects) so build_translation_index.py's numeric-unit lookup registers them as 'core'. Citizenship units should use SLUG filenames (e.g. b1-honfoglalas-01) exactly like LatAm's Spanish units do, so the existing dual-track machinery (scripts/build_translation_index.py's _track_for(), SLUG_TOPIC_LABELS) picks them up the same way — that script currently hardcodes track values 'core'/'latam' for ES B1 only, so it needs a small extension (a per-language track-name mapping, or simply reusing 'latam' as the internal track id with a language-appropriate display label) before HU B1 content lands. engine/drills/translation.js's TRACK enum and tab labels ('Core'/'Latin America') will need the same generalization to show 'Citizenship' under HU.

Citizenship-track units are a chronological history sweep (mirroring LatAm's chronological structure) ending in four dedicated civic units (constitution, government, holidays/symbols, being a citizen) — this maps directly onto what the actual honosítási interview tests: basic Hungarian history, the Alaptörvény, and national symbols/holidays.

Grammar pairing (checked directly against ES B1 before drafting this): the two tracks are NOT a strict 1:1 grammar match — Core unit 1 teaches the preterite specifically, while LatAm unit 1 teaches 'formal connectors' instead. Each LatAm lesson's grammar point is chosen to fit whatever construction best narrates that historical content (e.g. b1-economiacolonial-03 teaches the gerund because it fits "the expansion of plantations"; b1-revolucioncubana-02 teaches "acabar por + infinitivo" because it fits how a revolution concluded), while staying at the same overall B1 complexity and roughly tracking Core's pacing. Every unit below now carries its own `grammar` field on this same principle: Citizenship unit N's point is chosen to fit that historical/civic topic naturally, not cloned from Core unit N, though the two arcs are levelled to land on comparably complex structures around the same position in the sequence.

HU A2 already ends at 'Living in Hungarian' (past tense, future, conditional, storytelling, opinions/comparisons, problems/requests) — Core's early B1 units deepen and extend that rather than re-teaching it from scratch.

Vocabulary target per lesson (checked against ES B1's actual word counts, not pre-listed here — that's content-authoring work): Core ≈4 new words/lesson, Citizenship ≈8/lesson. Citizenship runs roughly double Core's vocab load, same ratio LatAm has against ES Core — matches TROUBLESHOOTING_BACKLOG.md's note that the cultural track 'is not a light cultural add-on, it's exactly as large as the Core grammar track.'

Reading structure (checked directly against ES B1's actual story files before deciding this): Core gets ONE reading per unit, inserted into the unit's last regular lesson — same one-per-unit pattern HU A1/A2 already use — but on ALL 36 units; ES's own Core only has 24/36 (units 1-11 and 36 have none), which looks like an incomplete build rather than a deliberate gap, so HU B1 should not repeat it. Citizenship instead replicates LatAm's actual (richer) model exactly: a SERIALIZED reading, one short segment (5-6 paragraphs) embedded in EACH of the unit's 5 regular lessons, plus a 6th standalone 'combined' version for the Library. Confirmed schema from content/es/stories/world/b1/b1-americalatinadosmil-*.json: files live under stories/world/<level>/ (not stories/original/), named <level>-<unit-slug>-<NN>-<slug-of-segment-title>.json for each per-lesson segment plus a bare <level>-<unit-slug>.json for the combined version; each segment carries id (story.b1.<unit-slug>.NN), title, level, lesson (which of the unit's 5 regular lessons it's embedded in, 1-5), order, type: 'world', estimatedMinutes, summary, characters (often [] for impersonal historical narration), location, grammar (array of the point(s) that segment's language draws on), and vocabularyTopics; the combined version reuses the same shape with lesson/order set to the unit's own overall position and pulls together all 5 segments' throughlines into one longer piece. HU's Citizenship track should follow this schema, under content/hu/stories/world/b1/ with slug filenames matching each unit's Hungarian topic (e.g. b1-honfoglalas-01-*.json).

citizenship.title: Citizenship
citizenship.description: A chronological sweep of Hungarian history plus dedicated civic units (constitution, government, symbols, holidays) — matches what the honosítási vizsga interview actually tests. Reuses Core's grammar rather than teaching its own; content filenames should be slug-based (e.g. b1-honfoglalas-01) like LatAm's Spanish units, not numeric, so the existing dual-track detection in scripts/build_translation_index.py picks them up correctly once extended for a third track name.
